name: Tessera Autonomous Rifle Platform TARP-3 'Delegate'
description:
The TARP-3 Delegate is an assault rifle designed to be wielded by humanoid combat drones rather than human operators. Tessera engineered every aspect of the weapon for machine operation — the grip pressure requirements exceed human hand strength, the trigger pull weight is set at 15 kilograms, and the manual of arms requires motor precision that only servos can deliver. A human can physically carry the Delegate but cannot effectively operate it.

The weapon fires 6mm caseless through a conventional gas system, but its fire-control is entirely machine-mediated. A hardened data port replaces the BCI link, connecting directly to the combat drone's targeting system. The Delegate achieves consistent sub-half-MOA accuracy at all ranges because the platform holding it does not breathe, flinch, or fatigue. Rate of fire is limited by the weapon's cyclic rate rather than the operator's trigger finger.

Tessera sells the TARP-3 exclusively as part of complete drone weapon systems, bundled with their combat automata. The weapon is useless without a drone, and the drone is less effective without its purpose-built weapon. This interdependency is deliberate — Tessera wants to sell platforms, not components.
specifications: caliber: 6mm caseless effective_range: 550m rate_of_fire: 800 rpm (cyclic) magazine_capacity: 40 rounds weight: 3.6 kg
tactical_use: The TARP-3 delivers inhuman accuracy from an inhuman platform. Combat drones carrying Delegates provide persistent, tireless fire support without risk to human operators. The machine-optimized design prevents field capture and use by human adversaries, ensuring that even if a drone is disabled, its weapon cannot be turned against friendly forces. Drone-Delegate teams are typically deployed in fire-and-forget perimeter defense roles.
cultural_context: The Delegate represents the dehumanization of combat taken to its logical extreme — a weapon that humans cannot use, carried by machines that cannot choose not to. Anti-autonomous weapons activists target the TARP-3 specifically because it is a rifle, the most human of weapons, redesigned to exclude humans entirely. Tessera's marketing avoids showing the Delegate in human hands, reinforcing the separation between people and the violence conducted on their behalf.
story_hooks: A technician has modified a Delegate to be human-operable by reducing the trigger weight and adding a conventional grip. The weapon's machine-precision accuracy is lost, but now a human can carry a rifle that corporate databases say only drones can use.

A combat drone carrying a Delegate has gone offline but continues to patrol its assigned route and engage targets. The drone's AI is damaged, and no one knows what its current targeting parameters are.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, purposefully alien assault rifle that reads as mechanically optimized rather than organically comfortable. The silhouette is sharp and geometric—no curves for human hands, no ergonomic forgiveness. It has the cold aesthetic of industrial machinery repurposed as a weapon, with an almost skeletal frame that prioritizes structural efficiency over intuitive handling.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 78 cm | Barrel length: 42 cm | Width at receiver: 8.5 cm | Magazine well depth: 6 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light at 3.6 kg—it feels hollow in human hands, almost fragile. The weight is distributed in ways that create an unbalanced, unsettling feel when gripped traditionally. Servo-grade loading points make it feel like it's waiting for something stronger.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade titanium alloy frame with reinforced polymer upper receiver. The construction prioritizes heat dissipation and cyclic durability over human comfort.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal grey with selective brushed titanium accents around the data port and fire control housing. Heat-treated sections show dark oxide patina. Everything is utilitarian—no aesthetic flourishes, only functional surface treatments.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey dominating, with deep charcoal polymer sections and brushed metallic silver highlights around the hardened data port. Accent lighting on control surfaces in cool cyan when powered.
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth, hard synthetic polymer—deliberately unfriendly to human skin. No stippling or grip texture. The magazine well is oversized and sharp-edged. The charging handle is a servo-actuated rod, not hand-operable.
distinctive_features: Oversized hardened data port (optical/electrical hybrid) mounted where a BCI connector would be on human weapons
15kg trigger pull assembly—visibly heavy spring housing
Servo access panels along the receiver side
Heat vents designed for drone mounting, not handheld operation
Caseless ammunition feed system with visible round staging
Ghost ring sights (non-functional for humans—purely aesthetic compliance)
Cyclic rate limiter visible as a mechanical governor on the bolt carrier
Asymmetrical charging handle—right-side servo rod only
Cable routing channels along the frame for drone integration hardpoints
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA logo stamped in steel relief on the upper receiver, small and clinical. Serial plate (titanium) mounted on the left side of the receiver with alphanumeric drone-pairing codes rather than traditional serial numbers. Fine print warning: 'MACHINE OPERATION ONLY' engraved in 4pt font along the lower receiver.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-pristine when deployed with new drones; accumulates carbon scoring and micro-abrasions from cyclic heat and mounting stress. No traditional wear patterns—damage appears as localized burn marks from sustained fire or servo mounting scars. Often shows installation marks from drone hardpoint coupling.
